title: Define and implement standardized overload error codes + JSON payloads (Gateway + downstream)
creator: Christine Wong
project: Reliability Program: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding
body:
## Context
We are introducing hosted circuit breakers + load shedding. Under overload, we need stable, customer-visible semantics (HTTP status + error code + retry guidance) instead of ambiguous timeouts/5xx. This task implements the standardized overload error taxonomy and payload shape across the API gateway and any downstream service that can reject requests (routing layer, runtime admission).

This is the “client contract” portion of the overload work and is referenced by ADR-014.

## Goals
- One canonical, stable overload error taxonomy and JSON payload shape.
- Same response structure regardless of where rejection occurs (gateway vs routing vs runtime) so clients do not need service-specific logic.
- Consistent Retry-After behavior to prevent retry storms.
- Correlation IDs present and documented (support + SRE debugging).
- Backwards compatible (additive fields).

## Non-goals
- Billing/credits policy changes (only wiring to usage enforcement if needed).
- SDK surface redesign beyond better typed errors + examples.

## Decision / Spec (per ADR-014)
### Status mapping (high level)
- 429: tenant-scoped limits (rate/concurrency) or policy-driven shed for fairness
- 503: platform capacity / dependency overload where retry may succeed soon

### Canonical JSON payload (additive)
All overload rejections must return JSON (even from gateway), with a stable error code and optional per-request fields.

Example (representative):
{
  "error": {
    "type": "overload_error",
    "code": "overload.shed",
    "message": "The service is temporarily overloaded. Please retry.",
    "retry_after_ms": 500,
    "request_id": "req_...",
    "correlation_id": "corr_...",
    "region": "us-east",
    "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
    "model": "redwood-verified/llama-3.1-70b"
  }
}

Notes:
- `message` is customer-safe and intentionally non-leaky.
- `retry_after_ms` is redundant with Retry-After header but included to make SDK handling easier. Header remains source-of-truth.
- `region/route/model` are included only when known at the rejection point; otherwise omitted.

### Headers
- Always set: `Content-Type: application/json`
- Always set: `X-Request-ID` (or preserve existing)
- Always set: `X-Redwood-Correlation-ID` (new if missing)
- When retry is appropriate: set `Retry-After` (seconds) and include `retry_after_ms` in payload

### Error codes (initial set)
- `overload.shed` — request rejected due to load shedding policy
- `overload.breaker_open` — circuit breaker open for route/model/region
- `overload.dependency_unhealthy` — downstream dependency brownout causing admission failure
- `overload.queue_full` — runtime/gateway admission queue at capacity

(Additional internal reasons may exist, but MUST map to one of the above stable codes.)

## Implementation plan
1) Implement shared overload error response struct + mapper from internal reasons → stable code/status.
2) Gateway: ensure admission middleware uses the shared response builder.
3) Routing/runtime: ensure any short-circuit paths use the shared response builder (or conforming equivalent) and propagate correlation IDs.
4) Tests:
   - Unit tests for mapper (status ↔ code)
   - Golden JSON response tests (payload shape is stable)
   - Integration: perf-canary scenario validates we see 429/503 with Retry-After rather than timeouts
5) Docs/support handoff: provide examples + retry contract snippet for SDK owners and Support.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Gateway overload responses match ADR-014 (status + JSON + code + headers)
- [x] Downstream overload responses match the same schema
- [x] Retry-After is consistently set when we expect clients to retry
- [x] Correlation ID appears in response and logs so Support can request it
- [x] SLO toolkit classification updated to classify overload errors distinctly from generic 5xx

## Rollout / risk
- Dark launch: emit metrics for “would-have-shed” vs “did-shed” (handled in ENG-4823/ENG-4826)
- Canary region: validate no client breakage (JSON parse, SDK handling), and verify Retry-After presence
- Known risk: inconsistent behavior if any legacy handler bypasses gateway middleware. Mitigation: add a lint/checklist item for routes and add a lightweight integration test.

## References
- ADR-014: Hosted overload error taxonomy
- ENG-4821: Epic (hosted circuit breakers + load shedding)
- Support enablement: “overload errors and retry guidance” doc
comments: 2025-10-29 (Christine Wong): Drafted initial code list + status mapping based on last week’s incident writeups. Keeping code set intentionally small; we can expand later but can’t retract without breaking clients. Sync with Nikhil to confirm customer-facing wording.

2025-10-31 (Ethan Park): Strong preference that gateway owns the final response shape (even if runtime rejects) to avoid drift. For runtime-initiated rejections, either bubble up a structured reason to gateway or share a response builder package. Please ensure correlation IDs are generated/preserved at the edge.

2025-11-03 (Nikhil Sharma): PM review — OK with 429 vs 503 split as proposed. Customer copy should avoid mentioning GPUs/queues. Add explicit guidance in docs: clients must respect Retry-After and apply exponential backoff with jitter.

2025-11-06 (Amara Diallo): Implemented shared error struct + mapping layer and wired gateway to use it. Added golden response tests. Open question: do we ever return 409 for idempotency conflicts under overload? Suggest no; keep out of scope for now.

2025-11-10 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure Retry-After is present in both 429 and 503 overload responses where retry is safe. Missing header is a known cause of retry storms. Add an alert/dashboard later for “overload response without Retry-After” (can follow up in ENG-4826).

2025-11-14 (Jordan Lee): Routing integration: we now preserve code + correlation_id when the router rejects due to breaker-open. Verified we’re not leaking internal reason strings. One concern: model/route fields may be unknown at gateway admission time; OK to omit but keep schema stable.

2025-11-19 (Amara Diallo): PR 18421 merged. Follow-up PR 18472 adds consistent Retry-After and a short internal ‘client retry contract’ comment block for SDK owners. Confirmed responses are JSON on all paths we hit in staging.

2025-11-26 (Aisha Bello): Closed out after verifying SLO-toolkit classification (overload errors separated from generic 5xx). Next step is to validate in canary with real SDK traffic and confirm Support has correlation ID lookup flow.
